title: God Meets Us in Our Weakness

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Lot said to them, "No, my lords, please! Your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have shown great kindness to me in sparing my life. But I can't flee to the mountains; this disaster will overtake me, and I'll die..." - Gen 19:18-20a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even now, rescued from a burning city, Lot argues. God said flee to the mountains; Lot protests, "I can't." His faith is small, his fear is large, and he asks to run to a nearby town instead. It's not an impressive moment. Lot has been dragged out by the hand and still he's negotiating, still afraid, still weak.

Yet notice that Lot does one thing right: he acknowledges God's grace. "Your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have shown great kindness to me." Even in his fear and faltering, he knows he has been shown mercy he didn't earn. Weak faith can still recognise grace.

And here is the wonder of what follows: God accommodates Lot's weakness. As the next verse shows, God grants his request. He does not thunder, "Do as I say or perish!" He bends toward Lot's fear and gives him the smaller mercy he asks for. God meets His faltering children where they are.

This is deeply comforting for all of us who follow God with weak and trembling faith. He is not harsh with our fears. He "knows how we are formed, he remembers that we are dust" (Ps 103:14). Jesus would not break "a bruised reed" or snuff out "a smoldering wick" (Matt 12:20). Bring your weak, fearful, faltering faith to God. He is gentle with it, and He meets you in your weakness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you fear God is harsh with your weak and faltering faith?
- Can you bring your fears honestly to a gentle God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, my faith is often weak and my fears are large. Thank You that You are gentle with me, remembering I am dust. Meet me in my weakness, and be patient with my faltering trust in You.
Amen.
